newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London closed easier as a burst of selling near the close overwhelmed the few buyers that were around. There was no news behind the sell-off. Near March lost $1.40 a tonne to close at $301.80, while May lost $1.60 to close at $302.30 per tonne. In New York raw sugar futures closed a heavily-traded session near the day's highs, as the funds covered short positions in March, fuelling the contract to a nearly one-month high. The action carried the spot contract over several levels of resistance to end at 10.69 cent/lb, up 23 points. May added 18 points to close at 10.72 cents/lb. The outer months gained 13 to 16 points. As the rise was not backed by fundamentals the market is unlikely to go up much further and it remains to be seen whether present levels can be held.

THAILAND - According to preliminary figures Thailand exported 4.492 million tonnes of sugar, raw value, in 1995/96 up from 3.847 million tonnes exported in 1994/95 and 2.802 million tonnes in 1993/94. Given expectations of a larger crop in 1996/97 exports could rise further this season if markets can be found.

GERMANY - The German Sugar Industry Association WVZ reduced its forecast of final beet deliveries in 1996/97 to 25.8 million tonnes from 26.4 million tonnes previously as the onset of winter weather and rain in some regions had made harvesting difficult as tractors got stuck in wet fields and night frost endangered plants in the ground. But more than two thirds of the crop had been harvested and were either being driven to factories or stored in the fields and covered. Sugar content remained fairly high at 18.14 per cent up from 16.73 per cent in 1995/96. Sugar production up to 15 November reached 2.847 million tonnes raw value, up from 2.587 million tonnes produced the same period 1995/96 and 2.664 million tonnes in 1994/95. The extraction rate reached 16.97 per cent, raw value, up from 15.51 per cent last year and 15.89 per cent in 1994/95.

NETHERLANDS - The Netherlands exported 287,825 tonnes of sugar, raw value, in October/July 1995/96 more than 20 per cent less than was exported the same period in 1994/95. Total exports in crop year 1994/95 (October/September) dropped to 381,586 tonnes from 654,277 tonnes the previous year. Major white sugar markets in October/July 1995/96 were Turkey (23,721 vs 28,815 tonnes), Libya (28,393 vs 17 tonnes) and Iran (61,805 vs 90,805). The country imported 50,487 tonnes of sugar, raw value, in October/July 1995/96 which compares to 47,817 tonnes the same period in 1994/95. Total imports in crop year 1994/95 dropped to 64,568 tonnes from 79,854 tonnes the previous year.

UK - The UK imported 1.219 million tonnes of sugar, raw value, in October/August 1995/96 8 per cent less than was imported the same period in 1994/95. Total imports in crop year 1994/95 (October/September) reached 1.468 million tonnes up from 1.336 million tonnes imported the previous year. Exports in October/August 1995/96 reached 361,020 tonnes 33 per cent less than was exported the same period 1995. Total exports in crop year 1994/95 rose to 560,076 tonnes up from 537,317 tonnes the previous year.Z
Zimbabwe tendered to buy 28,000 tonnes of raw sugar for arrival in two shipments in January and February. Results of the tender were not immediately available.
